messages:
anya: Heads up — p99 tail spike on /generate observed after the deployment at ~03:00 UTC. Numbers: p50 steady, p95 +12%, p99 +28%. I traced hosts and it looks host-side tokenization + streaming chunking are significant.

simon: Any flamegraphs or traces?

anya: Quick profile excerpt from perf-runner: 
```
CPU: tokenize() 24.1%
CPU: request_parse() 14.8%
CPU: grpc_writev() 11.9%
CPU: kvcache_eviction_path() 9.3%
CPU: kernel_selector.choose() 6.7%
```
Small sequences (median 6 tokens) are dominating traffic for this route.

kevin: Hmm, kernel_selector currently picks kernel based on avg seq_len and model dims. For tiny seqs that favors matmul_generic which is better for long seqs. We have matmul_smallseq that benchmarks ~18% lower latency for seq<=16 but selector isn't using the tail quantiles.

matt: KV cache numbers from stats: hit_rate went from 98% -> 72% after the rollout at 02:57. Eviction spikes correlate with host-preproc CPU spikes. kvstats snippet: 
```
route: /generate, shard: s3
qps: 420
hit_rate: 72% (was 98%)
evictions_per_min: 210
avg_kv_fetch_ms: 2.2
```

anya: Also seeing many tiny gRPC frames. gRPC writev isn't coalescing; we pay syscall for each chunk. Example logs: 
```
OUT: writev 1 {size=512}
OUT: writev 2 {size=128}
OUT: writev 3 {size=64}
```

kevin: Two action items: 1) fast path kernel selector change — use seq_len p90/p95 to choose smallseq kernel for routes dominated by short sequences, and 2) batching heuristic tweak — prefer max_batch_tokens adaptive by EWMA of observed seq_len distribution, not fixed max.

anya: Agreed. Also propose kvcache shard pinning for hot prefixes to avoid cross-shard eviction storms.

simon: For the gRPC side: increase in-memory coalesce buffer in proxy (GRPC_WRITEV_COALESCE_MS=2 -> 6ms) and bump MAX_FRAME_SIZE for streaming (from 64k -> 256k) should reduce writev counts. We should canary both.

kevin: I ran a quick synthetic canary locally: changed selector to use p95 -> chose matmul_smallseq, batching EWMA enabled, results: 
```
baseline p99 latency: 420ms
patched p99 latency: 350ms (-16.7%)
cpu tokenize down 14%
kv hit_rate improved to 91% (with shard pinning sim)
```

perf-bot: Canary report: canary-7821: host-side p99 -15.4%, kernel smallseq usage +42% for /generate, grpc writev count -63%.

matt: Nice. What's the rollout plan? Small change surface but touch serving runtime + proxy + kvcache config. Needs coordinated deploy.

anya: Plan proposal: 
- Phase 1 (canary): selector + batching config to 5% of traffic on staging canary. proxy coalesce flag off for canary A, on for canary B.
- Phase 2: monitor p50/p95/p99, kvcache hit_rate, and syscall counts for writev. 30 min steady window required.
- Phase 3: roll to 100% if no regressions, otherwise auto-fallback to previous kernel selector.

kevin: I'll open PR for selector change (ref: kernel-selector: use p95 heuristic + route override). Add unit tests for seq length histogram -> kernel mapping.

matt: I'll add kvcache shard-pinning feature flag and a small metrics dashboard for evictions per shard.

anya: I'll coordinate canary, watchstack during rollout and prepare rollback playbook.

simon: Quick checklist: telemetry tags (kernel_name, batch_size, seq_len_p95, writev_count) need to be emitted per request route. If we lack any, add here before canary.

anya: Sounds good. I'll create the follow-up ticket and tag you all. TL;DR: kernel selection + adaptive batching + gRPC coalesce + kvcache pinning -> expected host-side p99 drop ~15% and cost reduction.

kevin: Also note fallback path — if selector fails to find matching kernel, prefer matmul_smallseq for seq<=32 to be safe.

perf-bot: Action items added: #3489 kernel-selector, #3490 batching-ewma, #3491 kvcache-pinning, #3492 grpc-coalesce-tune.

anya: Thanks — will link PRs in the ticket. :thumbsup:

simon: I'll standby for canary logs and help with telemetry dashboards.

kevin: I'll push a draft PR in ~30m.

matt: Will instrument evictions dashboard by EOD.
